title: The README, Read Cold
subtitle: What a reader with no memory of the work could learn from README.md and the paths it names, checked claim by claim against the code.
bottom_line: A cold reader can say roughly what ARCS does but cannot run it, and four of the README's claims are wrong. Fix 1 puts one plain line, one checkable proof and a working way to try it on the first screen.
alias_note: Our own repo, audited on its human entry point. CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and WORLD.md are written for agents and were out of scope.
repo_private_note: The repo is private, so the source link works only for people with access.

labels.anchor_label: README claims the repo backs in full
labels.pack_line: Built from one 48-line README, the paths it names, and two live pages, with no transcript.
labels.leak_lede: Paths and features the README named that a reader could not find as described. This is a pointer gap, not a grade.

leaked_paths: _CANON/WORLD.md (the file is at the repo root)
operators/ as the L0-L5 pipeline (its own README says it is not wired into the live compass)
the Observatory replaying any decision (src/app/observatory/page.tsx holds a fixed dataset about the build itself)
SQLite in development (prisma.config.ts and src/lib/db.ts use Postgres in every environment)
anchors.leak_note: 9 of 20 claims check out in full, 7 hold in part, 4 are wrong. The wrong ones are pointers and setup facts, not product behavior.

self_authored_note: Source: the README was written by the same team it describes. The repo shows the code exists, not that the description is complete.

sections.name: What ARCS is
sections.headline: A question goes in, a bearing comes out, recorded as a receipt.
sections.shows: POST /api/compass makes one Claude call and writes a Receipt row (src/app/api/compass/route.ts lines 355 and 539). Anonymous callers are allowed under ADR-016, rate limited to 10 a minute.
sections.not_shown: Plain meanings for bearing, terrain, DEWY and Y-gate. The cold reader could not decode them.
sections.raise: One plain sentence first, and every term expanded on first use.

sections.name: How it works
sections.headline: DEWY and the Y-gate are real code; the stage list, the state list and the Observatory replay are described more strongly than they run.
sections.shows: src/lib/ygate.ts sets six states (GREEN, YELLOW, FORK, PARADOX, DELTA, SCRATCH), and tests/unit/ygate.test.ts runs 17 tests, all passing. The DEWY receipt schema is in runtime/specs.
sections.not_shown: Six separate stages: L0 to L5 is one Claude call with a staged prompt, and its L3 is a premise check, not a cascade. RED is a warning level that becomes DELTA, not a state. The Observatory replays a fixed dataset about the build, not a user's decision.
sections.raise: Describe the pipeline as one call with a staged prompt, and the Observatory as a demo of the build's own history.

sections.name: Run it
sections.headline: The Python CLI exists and uses only the standard library, but the README gives no input to feed it and no way to start the web app.
sections.shows: scripts/arcs_cli.py has the six verbs and imports only stdlib modules. scripts/score_me.py runs with no arguments.
sections.not_shown: A sample input. Run from the repo root, the example *.json picks up package.json and tsconfig.json. No npm install, env vars or database step for the web app.
sections.raise: Lead with the web app (live link plus local setup from package.json and src/lib/env.ts) and a test command that passes, and mark the CLI as needing scan files.

sections.name: Stack
sections.headline: Next.js 16, Prisma 7, Auth.js v5 and the Anthropic SDK are right; SQLite in development is not.
sections.shows: package.json lists each, and globals.css is the one stylesheet.
sections.not_shown: SQLite anywhere. prisma.config.ts says there is no SQLite fallback, and src/lib/db.ts throws if DATABASE_URL is unset.
sections.raise: Say Postgres in every environment, and list DATABASE_URL in setup.

sections.name: Repo topology
sections.headline: Four of six rows point the right way; two are wrong.
sections.shows: src/app, src/lib/ygate.ts, _DECISIONS (93 files) and runtime/specs hold what the table says.
sections.not_shown: WORLD.md in _CANON (it is at the root). A 34-file operator library (46 top-level .py files), presented as the live pipeline although its own README says it is not wired in.
sections.raise: Fix the WORLD.md path, drop the count, and label operators as a reference library.

sections.name: Live
sections.headline: arcs.care and app.arcs.care both load.
sections.shows: Both return HTTP 200. The app's compass opens at /dashboard with no account, and an example brief is linked from the home page.
sections.not_shown: That full access opens in stages behind a waitlist, which the live page says and the README does not.
sections.raise: Say what a visitor gets today: the compass without an account, the waitlist for more.

unverified.claim: The repo topology says WORLD.md lives in _CANON/.
unverified.why: _CANON/WORLD.md does not exist; WORLD.md is at the repo root.

unverified.claim: The stack uses SQLite in development and Postgres in production.
unverified.why: prisma.config.ts says there is no SQLite fallback; both environments use Postgres.
operators/ has 46 top-level .py files today; the 34 comes from its own README, also stale.

unverified.claim: operators/ holds L0-L5 as atomic components.
unverified.why: operators/README.md says it is not wired into the live compass route or any deployed surface.

unverified.claim: The Observatory replays any decision as a kinematic trajectory.
unverified.why: src/app/observatory/page.tsx renders a fixed dataset about the build's own history; no code path loads a user's receipt into it.

unverified.claim: The pipeline runs six stages, signal to global.
unverified.why: The compass route makes one Claude call; the stages are sections of its prompt.
src/lib/ygate.ts numbers 10 checks (1 to 6, 8, 9, 10, 12); 7 and 11 are absent.
src/lib/ygate.ts uses RED as a warning level and maps it to DELTA; the states it sets are GREEN, YELLOW, FORK, PARADOX, DELTA and SCRATCH.

unverified.claim: The CLI examples run the full five-verb pipeline.
unverified.why: They need scan JSON files the repo does not ship; *.json at the root matches config files.

unverified.claim: score_me.py produces a single-contact forensic receipt.
unverified.why: It applies fixed constants to a name, title, company and year, reads no data, and prints a link to the private repo.

unverified.claim: A reader can run the web app from the README.
unverified.why: No install, env var, database or dev-server step is given; they exist in package.json and src/lib/env.ts.

unverified.claim: Every architectural decision has a receipt.
unverified.why: 93 ADR files exist; whether every decision got one cannot be checked from the record.

unverified.claim: A cold reader reaches the stated understanding.
unverified.why: One agent (Sonnet) given only the README, plus the auditor's checks. Not a human panel.

unverified.claim: The compass returns a bearing for a real question.
unverified.why: Not exercised: a compass call spends API tokens. The live checks were HTTP status and page text.

run_note: One cold reader and no paid calls. A rerun with a human reader and one compass call would check both; these are limits of this run, not gaps in the README.

fixes.fix: Open with one plain line of what ARCS is, one proof a reader can run (the 17 Y-gate tests), and the live compass link that needs no account.
Correct the four wrong claims: the WORLD.md path, SQLite in development, operators as a reference library with no count, the Observatory as a demo of the build's own history.
Add local web-app setup taken from package.json and src/lib/env.ts: install, env vars, database, dev server.
Describe the gate as the checks and states it really has, not a 12D manifold with RED, and say the CLI needs scan files the repo does not ship.
Replace universal words like every with counts, and label score_me.py as a demo.

limits: It reads only the README and what it names. The agent-facing files were out of scope on purpose.
It is not a code review. It checks whether each README claim points at something real.
It never rates people. It reads the record, not the team.
repo_shape: one README, 48 lines, 20 claims checked, 2 live pages fetched
self_review_note: The auditor is an agent working in this repo; the cold reader was a separate agent given only the README.
